semantic_adjudication.basis: NL4.2 text, PlantUML line 17 raw label ('human steering cmd\\nor brake pressed\\nor in (auto final)'), fcstm_model event declaration (event:human_steering_cmd_nor_brake_pressed_nor_in_auto_final:line:5 as single opaque event), transition:line:26 trigger field, PlantUML label semantics (single trigger per transition label).
semantic_adjudication.reason: PlantUML line 17 declares: AutonomousMode --> HumanDrivingMode : human steering cmd\nor brake pressed\nor in (auto final). The closed model interprets this entire text as a single opaque event (event:human_steering_cmd_nor_brake_pressed_nor_in_auto_final:line:5). PlantUML transition labels have the form trigger [guard] / effect; a list of conditions separated by 'or' within one label is not decomposed into multiple triggers. Consequently, none of the individual conditions (human steering cmd, brake pressed, in auto final) can trigger the transition on its own. NL4.2 describes these as alternative conditions ('when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)') implying any one should suffice. The strongest rebuttal ('the closed model is consistent with itself') does not address the NL contract: self-consistency of the model does not establish that it matches the author's stated requirements. The semantic violation is that the model's trigger granularity is coarser than the NL requires.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: Each condition that may trigger AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode (human steering cmd, brake pressed, in auto final) must be a separately triggerable event or guard, as implied by NL4.2's listing of alternative conditions.

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL4.2 text, PlantUML line 17 raw label ('human steering cmd\\nor brake pressed\\nor in (auto final)'), fcstm_model event declaration (event:human_steering_cmd_nor_brake_pressed_nor_in_auto_final:line:5 as single opaque event), transition:line:26 trigger field, PlantUML label semantics (single trigger per transition label).
semantic_adjudication.reason: PlantUML line 17 declares: AutonomousMode --> HumanDrivingMode : human steering cmd\nor brake pressed\nor in (auto final). The closed model interprets this entire text as a single opaque event (event:human_steering_cmd_nor_brake_pressed_nor_in_auto_final:line:5). PlantUML transition labels have the form trigger [guard] / effect; a list of conditions separated by 'or' within one label is not decomposed into multiple triggers. Consequently, none of the individual conditions (human steering cmd, brake pressed, in auto final) can trigger the transition on its own. NL4.2 describes these as alternative conditions ('when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)') implying any one should suffice. The strongest rebuttal ('the closed model is consistent with itself') does not address the NL contract: self-consistency of the model does not establish that it matches the author's stated requirements. The semantic violation is that the model's trigger granularity is coarser than the NL requires.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: Each condition that may trigger AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode (human steering cmd, brake pressed, in auto final) must be a separately triggerable event or guard, as implied by NL4.2's listing of alternative conditions.

branches.reason: The behavior_consequence lens identifies two critical findings from the closed model. First, the root composite's initial entry to HumanDrivingMode (transition:line:28) carries a Power_On trigger, making it conditional rather than a true unconditional initial entry. Verify facts explicitly refute this as a valid initial entry, and the reference inspection confirms W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING. The behavioral consequence is a bootstrap failure: the system has no active state at startup, so Power_On has no reachable consumer to process it. Second, this directly causes the Power_On event to have zero reachable consumers (verified by the refuted event-consumer check), meaning the power-on signal can never be operationally received. All other contracts (declaration, endpoint, termination) are behaviorally satisfied in the closed model: HumanDrivingMode is simple, AutonomousMode is composite with sub-states, the HumanDrivingMode→AutonomousMode transition exists, the AutonomousMode→HumanDrivingMode path is achievable through the route-control compilation, Power Off reaches the root final state, and the final pseudostate has no outgoing continuations (stable termination).
